packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-11 - unverified image-only reading
Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this packet. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules (Read for brief/PROMPT/images, Write/Edit for this file).

LAYOUT SURVEY (from image-001.jpg, reduced overview)
- image-001 shows one face of a single sheet, landscape, photographed on black with a colour card (left) and a ruler (right). A vertical fold/gutter runs down the middle, so the face shows two half-pages (left half and right half) side by side. Damage: holes and dark stains in the upper right, upper edge cropped/abraded, heavy red offset/staining across the whole surface.
- Observation: each half-page is a tabular layout in red and black. From the left: narrow columns of small roman numerals (black and red), then a column of single letters (a-g sequence, black, with some red), then a wide text column with short entries beginning "S." (saint-type entries, mostly black, some lines in red), then a column of red roman numerals (repeated "xvi", "xv" etc.), then a narrow column of small black numerals/marks (".j.", ".ij.", "xix", "xviij").
- Right half: column of red/black letters (f g h i k l m n o p q r s t v ...), then several columns of black roman numerals under headings written vertically at top (one appears to read "Dienstag"?-like word written vertically; uncertain), then the a-g letter column, then the text column with entries ("S. ..."), some in red.
- Headings: vertical/rotated words at the top of the left half (partly cropped) and right half; a red heading line at the top of the right half text area ("...").
- Tentative interpretation: calendar-type table with vernacular (German-looking) entries. Not inferring date or provenance.
- Language of entries appears vernacular (e.g. "ein bischof", "marteler"), not Latin.

TRANSCRIPTION
Line numbers count rows of the table from the top of each image. Columns separated by " | ". Small red letters/numerals above or beside black numerals in the narrow left columns are given in {red: }.
